summary: Public observation tower in Dover's Garrison Hill park; the current iron tower was built by volunteers in 1993 on a summit with towers since 1880. FFLA lists it as an observation tower.

facts.design: 76-foot iron observatory, painted green; third tower on the summit

staffing.status: no fire-service staffing recorded in the sources; the tower serves the public park

access.note: City park open to the public. The road leads to a parking area at the summit, and a footpath leads to the tower.

visit.trail_note: Park road off Route 9 in Dover, about 0.9 miles north of Route 4. Parking area at the summit, then a footpath to the tower and its deck.

events.note: Wooden 65-foot observatory on the hilltop, opened to the public as a park and observatory (built or bought by Harrison Haley; sources differ)
City acquired the property and kept it as a public park
Steel tower commissioned by Abby Sawyer in memory of her husband
Park added to the National Register of Historic Places on September 11, 1987
Steel tower taken down for safety reasons
Current 76-foot iron tower built by volunteers (1993 per Wikipedia; the Dover page gives no year)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as an observation tower. NH Family Hikes says whether it was ever used as a fire tower is a matter of debate. The Wikipedia and Dover sources describe a public park observatory and do not mention fire work. The story calls it an observation tower and does not claim fire service. The editor may wish to review whether it belongs in the fire-lookout set at all.
Wikipedia says Haley purchased the 65-foot wooden observatory; the Dover page says Haley built it for $1000. The story says the sources differ.
Wikipedia dates the current tower to 1993. The Dover page and NH Family Hikes say volunteers built it and give no year. The story uses 1993 and attributes it to Wikipedia.
Sources spell the donor's name Abby (Dover) or Abbey/Abbie (Wikipedia). The story uses Abby Sawyer, as the city page does.

notes_for_editor: The record's kind 'tower' is kept, but the sources describe a public park observatory. FFLA lists it as 'Obs Tower', and NH Family Hikes says whether it was ever a fire tower is a matter of debate, so the editor should decide whether it belongs in the fire-lookout set. The 1880 to 1913 history rests on Wikipedia and the Dover page, which agree on the main events. The 1993 date comes only from Wikipedia. Leads: the NRHP nomination for Garrison Hill Park and Tower (NRHP No. 87001413), which Wikipedia cites and which would confirm the 1880s ownership and the 1990 and 1993 dates; and any City of Dover record of fire-tower use, if one exists.
